title: test(fields): cover PhoneField in the standard-widget suite, point DateField and TextAreaField to theirs
body:
Fixes #7336

Clause-②: no

Determined from this diff, not assumed: it is two files — `packages/fields/src/standard-widgets.test.tsx` and one changeset. It moves no declaration, adds no export, and touches nothing outside this package's own test suite.

## Summary — one widget got cases, two got pointers

The card asks whether `standard-widgets.test.tsx` hides a gap by covering 7 of the 10 standard widgets it once imported. It does. But the honest repair is **not** three cases, and it is not the two-cases-and-a-comment the triage ruling projected either. Measured per widget:

| widget | verdict | why |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `PhoneField` | **2 new cases** | the real gap |
| `DateField` | **pointer comment** | fully covered by a sibling file |
| `TextAreaField` | **pointer comment** | seven dedicated suites |

## The measurement, and where it departs from triage

Triage read one column: dedicated suites in `packages/fields/src/widgets/__tests__/`. That directory-scoped instrument was lit (`TextAreaField` scores 7 in it), but its **domain does not contain the coverage** — `CurrencyField`, the calibration control the card itself names, also scores **0** in that same directory while being covered in two other places. So I widened the instrument to "which test files anywhere actually render the widget", pathspec-filtered:

```
$ git grep -l '[OPEN-TAG]DateField' -- '*.test.ts' '*.test.tsx'
packages/fields/src/__tests__/date-locale-channel.test.tsx
packages/fields/src/datetime-widgets.test.tsx
```

(`[OPEN-TAG]` stands in for the JSX open-angle-bracket, which GitHub's body sanitizer eats.)

Per-widget counts on that instrument, with the controls printed in the same pass:

| widget | test files rendering it |
|:--|--:|
| `TextAreaField` | 12 |
| `CurrencyField` (control) | 5 |
| `DateField` | 2 |
| `EmailField` (control) | 2 |
| `UrlField` (control) | 2 |
| `PhoneField` | **1** |

**`DateField` is not the gap.** `packages/fields/src/datetime-widgets.test.tsx` — the file directly next to this one — already covers it. Brace-matched against the tree rather than eyeballed: its `describe('DateField')` spans lines 23-48 and holds exactly four cases — edit-mode input, onChange, locale-formatted readonly, empty-value dash. The objectui#3127 stored-ISO round trip for `DateField` is at line 153 in that same **file** but a **sibling** block, `describe('existing values round-trip through the native controls (#3127)')` at lines 88-164, which it shares with three `DateTimeField` cases. The locale channel is pinned separately in `__tests__/date-locale-channel.test.tsx` (objectui#4468) and the `toDateInputValue` helper in `widgets/nativeDateValue.test.ts`. Writing the readonly/edit round trip here would have duplicated it almost line for line — precisely the trap triage flagged, just attached to a different widget than expected.

**`PhoneField` is the gap.** It renders in exactly one test file, `__tests__/validation-feedback.test.tsx`, and all four of its cases there belong to a cross-widget contract battery: aria-invalid, disabled, empty-readonly dash, default placeholder. Nothing in that file — or anywhere else — asserted the two things that make it a phone widget: the `tel` input type, and the `tel:` link its readonly branch renders. The `tel:` assertions that do exist in the repo belong to the plugin-list and plugin-report **cell** renderers, not to this widget.

So `PhoneField` gets the readonly/edit round trip, in the shape the `EmailField` and `UrlField` blocks above it already use. No new shape invented.

## Verification

Exit codes were captured by redirect-then-read, never through a pipe; the verdict lines below are the gates' own output.

**Test counts, before and after** (repo root, as the objectui#3378 guard requires):

| run | files | tests |
|:--|--:|--:|
| `standard-widgets.test.tsx` before | 1 passed | **24** passed |
| `standard-widgets.test.tsx` after | 1 passed | **26** passed |
| whole `packages/fields/` after | 132 passed | 2152 passed |

The package-level *before* (132 / 2150) is derived, not directly measured: only one test file changed, and its own before/after was measured directly.

**Both new cases were shown to discriminate.** The fact was mutated in `PhoneField.tsx` — not the assertion — each mutation proven on disk by anchored fixed-string counts plus `git hash-object`, and each restore proven **by state** (`git diff HEAD` empty AND worktree blob equal to the HEAD blob), under `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths, restoring via `git checkout HEAD -- [abs path]`:

| mutation | result |
|:--|:--|
| `type="tel"` becomes `type="text"` | `Tests 1 failed \| 25 passed (26)` — only `should render tel input` |
| the `tel:` template href becomes the bare value | `Tests 1 failed \| 25 passed (26)` — only `should render clickable tel link in readonly mode` |

Each mutation kills exactly one case and only the intended one. Worth recording: mutation B's first attempt used an invalid regex for its anchored count, so the count came back empty — the script treated the void reading as a failure and aborted rather than reporting it, and the trap restored the tree. It was re-run with a fixed-string count.

**Gates, quoting their own verdict lines:**

- `check-changeset-presence.mjs` — first run exit 1, naming this file as published source of a released package. Its own text calls the empty-frontmatter declaration "the explicit exemption and a complete answer to this gate", which is what a test-only diff is; after adding it: `Every one of them has an EMPTY frontmatter — declared as releasing nothing`.
- `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` — `No changeset declares a major bump.`
- `tsc -p packages/fields/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — exit 0, 0 errors.
- `tsc -p packages/fields/tsconfig.test.json --noEmit` — exit 0, 0 errors. This one initially exited **2** with `TS2307 Cannot find module` across many files: a precondition, not a failure. After building the dependency closure it is clean. Confirmed by `--listFiles` that the edited file is genuinely in the program (1 hit) rather than excluded — a `typecheck` that excludes test files would have been a true statement about nothing.
- `eslint` on `packages/fields` — 214 files, **0 errors**, 913 warnings, none new in kind: the file's `as any` count goes 24 to 26, exactly the two added cases in the idiom every case in the file already uses.
- Control-byte self-scan over both touched files — clean.

**Narrowings, declared:**

- *eslint run over `packages/fields` (214 files by eslint's own enumeration) rather than the whole repo.* It could have caught a lint violation in a file this diff edits — and the one file this diff edits is inside those 214. The repo's `eslint.config.js` sets no `projectService` or `parserOptions.project`, so linting is not type-aware and no untouched file's verdict can move on account of this diff.
- *vitest run over `packages/fields/` rather than the full repo suite.* It could have caught a suite that consumes the changed file; `git grep` finds **zero** references to `standard-widgets` outside the file itself, with a lit control in the same pass (`widgets/PhoneField` returns 4+ referencing files, so the instrument works).
- *typecheck limited to this package's two tsconfigs.* It could have caught a consumer type break; the diff exports nothing and changes no type.

## Out of scope, filed not fixed

**#7570** — `openNativePicker` has zero test coverage anywhere in the repo, with `toDateInputValue` lit as the control on the same instrument. `DateField` is its sole router and no existing case fires a click. Recorded, unassigned; deliberately not fixed here, since this card is `p3` and scoped to one file's documentation-of-absence.

## Correction, pushed as a second commit

The pointer comment's first wording said `describe('DateField')` held the objectui#3127 round trip. It does not — the block holds four cases and the round trip sits in the sibling block named above. The file is still the right destination, but the comment named the wrong block inside it, and this card exists precisely because a suite asserted a shape it did not have. `b7f1b545d` corrects the comment text; no assertion changed, and the diff is still the same two files.

Re-verified on the new head `b7f1b545d`: `standard-widgets.test.tsx` 1 file / 26 tests passed, `check-changeset-presence.mjs` green (`declares 1 changeset(s)`), eslint on the file 0 errors / 26 warnings (unchanged), control-byte scan clean. The mutation battery was deliberately not re-run: the assertions are byte-identical, only comment prose moved.
